To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
estrogen treatment of LNCaP cells increased tubulin polymerization and decreased cell cycle progression in a concentration-dependent fashion.

estrogen effects on tubulin and microtubule dynamics in prostate cancer cells may contribute to the development of hormone refractory prostate cancer and that estrogen effects may be exploited to enhance the efficacy of microtubule targeted agents.

estrogens increase the polymerization of tubulin and the expression of tubulin in prostate cancer cells, that this increase in tubulin polymerization may be a mechanism by which estrogens induce cell death in these cells and that estrogens have synergistic cytotoxic effects with taxanes, possibly due to the increased tubulin levels induced by estrogen.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of estrogen on tubulin expression, cell cycle progression and taxane mediated cell killing in prostate cancer cells.
the development of novel taxane analogues and with the identification of novel targets for taxane based therapies.
the effect of the estrogenic compounds on tubulin expression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
estrogens modulate microtubule function in prostate cancer cells, but the mechanism is not yet clear.
estrogen treatment does not affect the microtubule structure or the tubulin protein expression, but it does affect the cell cycle progression.
estrogen receptor positive prostate cancer cell lines have a differential response to estrogen treatment and that the effects on tubulin are cell line specific.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

estrogens modulate the cell cycle and microtubule dynamics in prostate cancer cells by increasing tubulin expression, which may be related to the ability of estrogen to increase the efficacy of taxane based chemotherapy.
estrogen effects on tubulin gene expression and taxane cytotoxicity are complex.
estrogens do not change microtubules in prostate cancer cells, and that the effects of taxanes on tubulin are not modulated by estrogens.
The main takeaway from our work is that
estrogen can alter microtubule dynamics, which can be exploited to increase sensitivity of prostate cancer cells to microtubule-active agents.
